title: Grading Executable Legal Rules Against Independent Records: Transitional Provisions and Korean SME Status
abstract: arXiv:2611.24055v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Laws are increasingly turned into programs that decide cases, such as whether a firm was a small or medium enterprise (SME) on a given date, and large language models (LLMs) now write them. The programs are usually graded against answers written by someone who read the same law, so a program can score well by sharing the grader's reading rather than by getting the law right. LexTemporis grades them instead against records of what actually happened: 10,901 firm-years of SME status disclosed by Korean listed companies, with every version of the governing rules. An appendix adds comparison cases from US income tax and German hospital minimum volumes. The date changes outcomes mainly through provisions outside the main statutory text: one transitional provision raises agreement with the disclosures from 83-86% to 89-90%. translated_title: 基于独立记录评估可执行法律规则：过渡性条款与韩国中小企业身份认定
translated_abstract: 法律正日益被转化为能够决定具体案件的程序，例如判断一家企业在特定日期是否属于中小企业（SME），而如今大型语言模型（LLM）已经开始编写这类程序。这些程序通常通过与阅读同一部法律的人所写出的答案进行对比来评分，因此程序可能仅仅因为与评分者共享相同的法律解读而获得高分，而非真正正确地执行了法律。LexTemporis 则改用实际发生的事实记录来评估这些程序：即韩国上市公司披露的10,901个企业年度的中小企业身份认定结果，以及所有相关规则的历史版本。附录还补充了来自美国所得税和德国医院最低手术量规定的对比案例。研究发现，日期对结果的影响主要来自主法条文本之外的条款：其中一项过渡性条款使程序与披露记录的一致率从83-86%提升至89-90%。这些披露记录还检验了作者对一项有争议条款的解读，在189个相关企业年度中有130个支持该解读。
tldr: 提出LexTemporis方法，以韩国上市公司10,901个企业年度的中小企业身份披露记录等独立事实为基准评估法律执行程序，发现主条文之外的过渡性条款显著提升判定一致率（从83-86%升至89-90%），并可检验争议条款的不同解读。
en_tdlr: LexTemporis grades executable legal rules against independent real-world records—10,901 firm-years of Korean SME status disclosures—showing that transitional provisions outside the main statutory text significantly improve agreement (from 83-86% to 89-90%) and adjudicating contested interpretations.
